items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I had the pleasure of working with some musicians that I made friends with for life. One of them was a fellow everybody calls Christopher Columbus -- Chris Columbo.

ctx.x: But before that, we did a thing of recording for... I don't remember the record company we did it for. I think it was Decca. But we recorded for about a week, which included about, I guess, at least 18 or 20 sides, if I can remember, of just about everything that he'd ever done. He re-recorded a lot of the things. And while we were in New York, I think, we also did The Milton Berle Show, which was a very big show on television. So it wound up being a very successful thing.

During that period, I had the pleasure of working with some musicians that I made friends with for life. One of them was a fellow everybody calls Christopher Columbus -- Chris Columbo. He is a drummer, and I guess Chris should be in his middle seventies or close to eighty years old -- I understand he's still playing in Atlantic City. He had a very unique way of playing.
